newsitem.title: CHINA: China's biggest film maker wins preferential policies.
newsitem.headline: China's biggest film maker wins preferential policies.

text.p: China's biggest film manufacturer, China Lucky Film Corp, has won preferential policies from the government to help it compete against international giants, the People's Daily said on Wednesday.
Company officials refused to give details of the preferential policies.
"We have not yet decided what we can tell media and what we cannot," said an official reached by telephone at Lucky's headquarters in Baoding in northern Hebei province.
The announcement of preferential policies came during a visit by Premier Li Peng on Tuesday to the plant, which holds a 24 percent market share, the People's Daily said.
However, the Lucky official said the company was still in negotiation with its U.S. suitor and competitor Eastman Kodak Co on some form of cooperation. He declined to give details.

China Lucky has lost ground rapidly in recent years to Kodak and Japan's Fuji Photo Film Co. Fuji already occupies about 48 percent of the China market and Kodak occupies most of the rest of market share not held by Lucky.
Neither Kodak nor Fuji manufactures in China, and the U.S. giant has been eager to ensure a stronger foothold in the market, and to avoid high import tariffs, by manufacturing locally.
Lucky has said it would be willing to cooperate with Kodak but not at the cost of giving up control of the company or eliminating the brand from the market.
The firm has said it plans to list domestic A shares this year.
Premier Li reminded the company of the need to adapt to the marketplace, a common weakness among China's large state-owned firms.
